title: How the Syndicate sees itself
summary: The money Convention as hero of the Union.

claims.text: Syndicate members call the Avatar Storm the Dimensional Anomaly and say it severed the Union's head while the Masses grew ever more connected.
They claim to offer a level playing field and to protect consumers while showing the Masses how to play and what it will cost.
They see themselves as the earners who pay for the other Conventions' fight in the streets, and believe the war is being won.

title: Chairs
summary: Syndicate leaders seated in big organisations.

claims.text: A Chair is placed in a large corporation or criminal network to keep its power and infrastructure intact.
Chairs are also expected to show steady growth, such as an oil magnate moving into solar and gas, or a shipper turning to smuggling.
Syndicate work hands out great but fickle power with few rules, and agents can never be sure whether a task is Union business or someone's pet project.

title: Disbursements
summary: The money managers of the Technocratic Union.

claims.text: Disbursements funds the whole Union, so its displeasure can kill a project, while its favour brings money, talent and power.
It holds the Union's largest and safest Ventures, packaging Quintessence for use across the world in return for small favours.
It began at the Convention of the Ivory Tower when someone asked who would pay for the plans, and was first called the Sun Guild.
Enforcers rely first on persuasion, threats and blackmail, holding that the threat of force beats actual carnage.
Private security is their stronghold, with mercenary firms as fronts, organised crime their lasting frontier and industrial espionage a sideline.
They have thoroughly infiltrated law enforcement as well.

title: Financiers and the Proctor takeover
summary: The core of the Syndicate and how it took its modern form.

claims.text: Financiers found companies, mount hostile takeovers, lobby governments and break up firms when they are done with them.
In 1851 the tangle of guild laws was folded into one body named the Financiers.
With backing from Rathbone's new Ivory Tower, Reginald Proctor's cabal seized effective control of the Syndicate, ending the High Guild's role as a servant of the Order of Reason.
Early Media Control tried to take over newspapers but was rebuffed by press barons such as William Randolph Hearst.
That started a century-long push to replace newspapers with newsreels, broadcast news and finally the Internet.
Anonymous news is easier to steer, so Media Control likes that no one cares where Internet news comes from.
